thread:
Ana: Hey team — noticed a latency spike on small-batch decode on the canary cluster after yesterday's kernel selector default change. Prefill looks fine, decode tails are worse. Anyone else seeing this?
Sam: Yep, saw it around 15:40 UTC. P50 stable but P95/P99 jumped ~30-40ms on 8k models. :thinking_face:
Lee: I profiled a few traces: the decoder is falling back from fused-paged-attn -> flash-variant-B for seq_len=32 decode batches. That variant has an unexpected warp divergence on small batches.
Priya: Can you paste the perf snippet? curious about occupancy and l2 utilization.
Lee: Sure, from nvprof-like summary (redacted):
```
kernel: flash_var_b decode
avg_latency: 0.82ms (batch=4)
avg_latency: 1.25ms (batch=2)
sm_efficiency: 62%
l2_read_hit: 38%
registers_per_thread: 40
```
Fallback fused-paged path was doing ~0.55ms at batch=2. So interestingly fallback faster for tiny batches.
Ana: So the selector is choosing flash_var_b for decode because it wins on larger microbatches. But decode small-batch distribution is dominant for streaming traffic. Selector heuristic needs to be workload-aware.
Sam: Exactly. Current heuristic picks kernel based on estimated throughput at target seq_len distribution aggregated over last 10s. For decode we should bias for small-batch latency instead.
PerfBot: AUTOMATION: ran microbench across kernels on the canary GPU pool — attached summary link: http://perf/reports/1722223333 (internal) :robot_face:
PerfBot: Summary: flash_var_A best for prefill, flash_var_B best for large decode, fused-paged best for small decode (<batch 8) on Ampere.
Priya: Also found KV cache fragmentation causing extra copies in the decode path when page alignment differs between requests. The extra memcpy shows up in the timeline right before the kernel launch. That amplifies the latency regression.
Lee: Good catch — upload of KV pages is hitting the allocator's small-frag path. We should try coalescing small KV writes and align to 4KB boundaries in the allocator.
Ana: Quick mitigation idea: change selector policy for decode routes to prefer fused-paged for batch<=8; also add a short-term toggle to force fused for the problematic customer traffic.
Sam: I'll sketch a diff: add "contextual_policy: route_type" to kernel selector and a tunable threshold for decode-batch-size. Can we get a perf run with that toggle?
PerfBot: AUTOMATION: queued microbench with selector toggle ON for decode routes. ETA 12m.
Priya: For root cause: two factors — kernel-level warp divergence in flash_var_B on tiny batches + allocator KV fragmentation memcpy. Both together push P99 up. Separately they might have been acceptable.
Lee: I'll open a small PR to add alignment coalesce in kv_allocator and a metric to surface small-kv-write fraction per route.
Ana: Sounds good. Owners? Lee on allocator PR, Sam on selector policy, Priya to add timeline instrumentation and reproduce with a synthetic streaming workload. I'll coordinate canary toggles.
Sam: Draft selector change in my branch, will ping for review in ~45m. If canary with fused-paged for decode fixes P99, we can roll as a short-term rollback of the selector default.
Priya: Also worth running the same microbench on T4 and H100 pools — Flash variants behave differently across archs. I'll spin that up.
Ana: Thanks all. TL;DR: ramp a fused-paged preference for decode small-batches + fix kv allocator coalescing. If PerfBot can validate before the next deploy window we can avoid a rollback. :thumbsup:
Sam: noted. Will update thread with canary numbers.
PerfBot: AUTOMATION: microbench (fused-pref decode) complete: p99 down 45ms on canary, throughput stable. link: http://perf/reports/1722223333/canary-1
Ana: Nice. Schedule readiness check with eng-sre if the canary sustains for 30m.
Lee: PR 5482 opened: kv-align-coalesce, includes unit test & perf measurement.
Priya: Ran cross-arch run: H100 shows similar pattern but less severe; T4 prefers fused by larger margin. Adding arch-weighted fallback in selector seems prudent.
Ana: Perfect. We'll keep the fused-pref decode toggle for 24h, monitor logs, then merge selector policy change. Thanks everyone.
